headline: Recovering cell-state dynamics and periodic phase from untimed single-cell data
label: Computational Single Cell Dynamics Methods
summary: Untimed single-cell and multi-omic data are now modeled to recover periodic phase, latent dynamics, and causal regulatory structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of temporal or dynamic structure from single-cell and multi-omic data not collected as continuous time courses. CoPhaser separates cell-cycle, circadian and other periodic phases from cellular context in scRNA-seq, while DCPR reconstructs circadian phase from untimed transcriptomic data and outperforms existing methods on simulated data. GRAIL generates intermediate single-cell transcriptomic states between two developmental stages via LSH-guided latent interpolation with a GAN decoder, and ddHodge reconstructs gradient, curl and acceleration components of cell-state vector fields from sparse scRNA-seq. MoFlow infers expression kinetics from multi-omic relay velocity, and DANSE fits dynamic models to time-series multi-omics to nominate regulators. What is new is explicit modeling of latent phase or interpolated cell state within the data. IDEAL-Age, GenoME, GITIII and CausalGRN address adjacent, largely non-temporal questions of immunological aging, genomic profile prediction, spatial cell-cell interactions and causal regulatory networks.
